title: What Would Make Us Scale Up?
scene: Your team has completed a small pilot. The results look promising, and some members want to expand it immediately.
sceneJa: 小規模な試行で期待できる結果が出たが、すぐに全面展開せず、再現性と追加投資の判断基準を確認する場面。

chunks.ja: 小規模な実験では期待できる結果が出ました
しかし、慎重になる必要があります

chunks.en: not to scale up too quickly.
chunks.ja: 急いで規模を拡大しないように
確認する必要があります

chunks.en: whether the results can be repeated
chunks.ja: その結果を再現できるかどうか
異なる条件のもとでも
また、あらかじめ合意しておくべきです
どの程度の成果水準なら
追加投資の十分な根拠になるのかを

chunks.en: If the evidence meets those criteria,
chunks.ja: 根拠となるデータがその基準を満たしていれば

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: we need to check / whether the results can be repeated / under different conditions
we need / to check whether / the results can / be repeated under
we / need to check whether the / results can be / repeated under different
questions.explanation: Keep the question about repeatability together, followed by the conditions.

questions.question: What does ‘justify further investment’ mean?
options: Provide enough reason to invest more.
Explain why the pilot was delayed.
questions.explanation: Justify means provide a sufficient reason for an action.

questions.question: Why test under different conditions?
options: To make the pilot more expensive.
To see whether the results are repeatable.
questions.explanation: Results should be repeatable beyond the initial pilot setting.

speak: Read the final two sentences three times. Stress ‘what level of performance’ and ‘meets those criteria’. Sound careful, but not hesitant.
review: Previous lesson: ‘only if it can teach us something’, ‘what result would justify expanding it’, ‘the smallest test that still gives us meaningful evidence’. Today moves from useful pilot evidence to repeatability and criteria for scaling up.
